tips: Build new armies and fleets only in spring, at a supply centre you own — and never in the very first spring of the game.
Fortifying an area doubles its defence; a quiet province with strong walls beats a proud one with none.
Spy on an area before you attack it to reveal its garrison, but remember the report goes stale as the seasons pass.
Bribing a neutral country chips away at its garrison until it flips to your side — though it earns you no victory points.
Armies that march into the same area in the same turn fight together, so concentrate your forces.
Each fleet carries 1,000 troops and can only sail from port to port, so plan your landings around coastlines.
You must leave 1,000 troops behind when marching out of an area, so garrisons cost more than they appear to.
Conquering areas wins you victory points — check which ones are worth the most before you march.
Losing battles costs you victory points, so avoid the tempting folly of attacking everything.
Your income arrives every spring, so spend the winter planning and the spring spending.
An enemy that is losing listens to a peace offer, especially one with money in it. Every peace buys two years of truce.
Protect your supply centres: they are the only places your armies and fleets can be built.
Old spy reports are worse than no reports — always refresh your intelligence right before an attack.
Do not neglect your treasury: a rich power can bribe, loan, and outlast its rivals.
Bring armies home by sea when a front collapses: a fleet carries 1,000 troops for every ship.
Neutral countries in the Americas are tougher than they look; scout them before you march.
